newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper recovers to plus side by the close.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper recovers to plus side by the close.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended slightly higher on Monday after a round of trade buying nudged the market back into the plus column before the closing bell.
Dealers said industry-linked buying, along with some short-covering by speculators, spurred the last-minute rally, but they noted turnover remained fairly thin throughout the session.
COMEX September futures gained 0.30 cent a lb on the day, to close at 112.15, after trading from 110.60 to 112.70.

Most discussions focused on prompt tightness in the London market ahead of Wednesday's July options expiry. LME spot premiums widened further today, helping New York to regroup from back over the unchanged barrier by the close.
"This market is very attuned to the tightness for the July date in London," said one trader. "If the cash and July are firm, we may try and rally a bit."

But some dealers said that after last week's sharp 10-cent sell-off, any upside progress would be tough-going. Solid resistance was seen at 113 cents basis the September contract, while support was noted toward 110.50.
LME cash to three months backwardation remains strong at $142/$147. LME stocks Monday rose a nominal 250 tonnes to 125,150 tonnes.
Meanwhile, workers at Inco's Sudbury mine voted over the weekend to end their four-week strike. The Sudbury mine produces about 200 million pounds of copper annually and supplies the U.S. Northeast.
(( Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640))
